report_title: EY Four Trends Redefining Cash Management

executive_summary: The 2025 McKinsey Global Payments Report highlights a payments industry at a critical juncture, characterized by competing systems, rising digital assets, and the transformative impact of AI. Global payments revenue reached $2.5 trillion in 2024, projected to grow to $3.0 trillion by 2029, though growth is slowing due to shifting payment methods and interest rates. Key forces include increasing fragmentation and regionalization, the accelerated adoption of stablecoins, and AI's role in optimizing operations and enabling agentic commerce. For CMIplus, success will hinge on enhancing interoperability, leveraging AI for efficiency and client experience, and strategically integrating digital assets while prioritizing trust and programmable compliance in a multirail, contested landscape.

themes.name: Fragmentation and Regionalization of Payments Landscape
themes.description: The global payments ecosystem is entering an unprecedentedly complex phase, moving away from universal efficiency towards competing market systems. Geopolitical events and technological progress are driving regionalization, with countries promoting payments sovereignty and developing local instant payment infrastructures. This creates a multirail environment, either with global passkeys or escalated fragmentation, impacting cross-border flows and standards.
themes.key_stat: The global financial system is influenced by nonfinancial factors such as tariffs, data governance rules, energy constraints, and national security priorities. The growing divergence in payments reflects the evolution of the broader financial system into a mosaic of regions with different standards, timelines, currencies, and trust anchors.

themes.name: Accelerated Adoption of Stablecoins and Tokenized Money
themes.description: Stablecoins and tokenized money are becoming an increasingly important part of the financial system, with issuance doubling since early 2024. Regulatory clarity is increasing, lowering barriers for traditional financial institutions. They offer potential for real-time cross-border settlements, intraday liquidity, and programmable finance, but also pose risks to traditional deposit funding models if widely adopted as a held form of money.
themes.key_stat: Stablecoin issuance has doubled since early 2024—but its role in the broader global payments landscape remains somewhat limited. With daily transaction volumes around $30 billion, stablecoins still represent a fraction of the trillions of dollars transacted worldwide each day.

themes.name: Transformative Potential of Artificial Intelligence (AI)
themes.description: AI is reshaping payments by optimizing transaction routing, automating reconciliation/settlement, enhancing fraud detection, and improving software development. The rise of 'agentic AI' is creating a new battleground, allowing AI agents to operate independently to select, optimize, and transact on behalf of humans. This will impact customer journeys and payment orchestration, requiring new engagement models.
themes.key_stat: Recent McKinsey research found that 10 percent of consumers use Al to start their online shopping journey, and 20 percent would be comfortable asking Al to make a purchase on their behalf.

themes.name: Evolving Revenue Models and Cost Pressures
themes.description: Payments revenue growth is slowing to 4% annually, impacted by peaking interest rates and a structural shift towards lower-cost payment options like account-to-account (A2A) transfers and digital wallets. Ongoing pricing pressures, regulatory scrutiny, and platform-driven payment experiences are squeezing fee-based revenue models, necessitating the emergence of new economic and fee models.
themes.key_stat: In 2024, payments revenue growth slowed to 4 percent, a notable drop from the 12 percent increase in 2023.

themes.name: Importance of Interoperability and Ecosystem Play
themes.description: In a fragmented, multirail world, interoperability is no longer a differentiator but critical infrastructure. Players must bridge asset types, jurisdictions, and compliance regimes in real-time. Success means becoming a foundational layer within ecosystems, enabling others to build on intelligence, trust, liquidity, or connectivity, rather than operating in isolation. This requires flexible, open infrastructures.
themes.key_stat: Cross-border and multirail transactions will define any foreseeable future scenario. The ability to bridge asset types, jurisdictions, and compliance regimes in real time will no longer be a differentiator. Players will want adaptive infrastructure that supports this natively.

themes.name: Trust and Programmable Compliance as Differentiators
themes.description: As AI and automation increasingly initiate transactions, transparency, explainability, and error resolution must be designed into systems to build user and regulator trust. With diverging regulations, codifying local compliance into infrastructure through modular policy engines and region-specific logic will be crucial for scalable players, superseding manual workflows and hard-coded rule books.
themes.key_stat: As Al and automation increasingly initiate transactions, firms will want to ensure that transparency, explainability, and error resolution are designed into their systems, so that users and regulators can understand what happened and why.

key_actions.action: Enhance Multirail Interoperability and Regional Connectivity
key_actions.rationale: The report emphasizes fragmentation and regionalization. CMIplus serves international corporates in CEE with diverse channels (EBICS, H2H, SWIFT, Open API). Ensuring seamless interoperability across these and emerging regional instant payment systems is crucial to maintain competitiveness and support multi-currency payments for our clients.
key_actions.timeline: Ongoing, with immediate focus on CEE regional instant payment integration by Q4 2026.

key_actions.action: Integrate AI for Operational Efficiency and Enhanced Client Experience
key_actions.rationale: AI is a major force for optimizing transaction routing, reconciliation, fraud detection, and potentially enabling agentic commerce. CMIplus can leverage AI to improve its H2H and EBICS channels, automate corporate treasury workflows, and offer predictive insights, significantly enhancing its value proposition and reducing operational costs.
key_actions.timeline: Pilot programs for AI-driven fraud detection and reconciliation by Q2 2026, broader rollout by Q4 2027.

key_actions.action: Explore Stablecoin and Tokenized Money Integration for Corporate Use Cases
key_actions.rationale: Stablecoins offer potential for real-time cross-border payments, intraday liquidity, and programmable finance, which are highly relevant for large international corporates. CMIplus should investigate how to securely integrate stablecoin-based payments and treasury services, especially given increasing regulatory clarity and the potential for new revenue streams.
key_actions.timeline: Feasibility study and sandbox testing by Q3 2026, strategic roadmap by Q1 2027.

key_actions.action: Strengthen Trust and Programmable Compliance Frameworks
key_actions.rationale: In a complex, AI-driven, and fragmented regulatory environment, trust and transparent compliance are paramount. CMIplus needs to ensure its systems are designed for explainability, error resolution, and adaptable to local CEE regulations, potentially through modular policy engines for ISO 20022 and other standards, to maintain client confidence and regulatory adherence.
key_actions.timeline: Implement enhanced audit trails and explainability features for AI-driven processes by Q3 2026, develop modular compliance engine roadmap by Q2 2027.

competitive_implications: The payments landscape is shifting from universal efficiency to a competition of diverse systems, driven by fragmentation, digital assets, and AI. CMIplus must proactively adapt by enhancing interoperability across traditional and new rails, leveraging AI for efficiency and client value, and exploring digital asset integration to avoid being disintermediated by agile fintechs or larger global platforms. Maintaining trust and offering programmable compliance will be key differentiators in this evolving, multirail ecosystem.

executive_summary: This 10th anniversary edition of 'Journeys to Treasury' highlights a decade of treasury evolution, emphasizing a renewed focus on fundamental competencies like cash flow forecasting and liquidity visibility. Digital transformation, driven by AI, virtual accounts, and real-time payments, is reshaping operations and demanding new skills. Regulatory changes, particularly Instant Payments and Verification of Payee (VoP), introduce both opportunities for efficiency and challenges in fraud prevention and data standardization. Treasurers are increasingly adopting a strategic role, leveraging data and automation to become proactive partners, but face hurdles in legacy systems, talent gaps, and organizational alignment. The report underscores the critical need for patience, practicality, and collaboration among all stakeholders to build sustainable, future-proof treasury functions.

More than a quarter of treasurers (27.6%) list fraud prevention as a priority.
17% of corporates now use virtual accounts primarily for reconciling incoming payments.

38.7% of treasurers identify ESG reporting as their top regulatory concern.
Reviewing and replacing treasury technology infrastructure is the third-highest priority.

themes.name: Cash Flow Forecasting & Liquidity Visibility
themes.description: Cash flow forecasting has returned as the top priority for treasurers, driven by macroeconomic volatility and geopolitical uncertainty. Many existing models still rely on semi-manual processes, highlighting the urgent need for reliable short-term and rolling forecasts. Accurate liquidity visibility is crucial for working capital optimization, funding strategies, and risk management, yet inaccurate forecasting remains a significant challenge for centralization efforts.
themes.key_stat: almost one in three treasurers (30.5%) prioritising forecasting the most.

themes.name: Payments Modernization & Regulation
themes.description: The payments landscape is undergoing rapid transformation due to the EU Instant Payments Regulation, ISO 20022 migration, and the introduction of Verification of Payee (VoP). These changes promise real-time liquidity, enhanced fraud prevention, and structured data, but also bring new compliance demands, operational complexities, and the need for system adaptations. Corporates must prepare for a more interconnected payment environment, with a focus on master data quality and system readiness.
themes.key_stat: 20% of respondents have already implemented real-time payments, and another 34% plan to do so soon.

themes.name: Automation & Digital Transformation
themes.description: Treasurers are actively pursuing digital transformation, starting with foundational elements like systems, data, and skills. While interest in advanced analytics, real-time reporting, and robotics is surging, many are still addressing legacy systems and fragmented architectures. AI is moving from hype to practical applications in forecasting, compliance, and workflow automation, but its successful adoption hinges on clean, well-structured data and a modular approach to building use cases.
themes.key_stat: Reviewing and replacing treasury technology infrastructure is now the third-highest priority

themes.name: Talent & Cultural Shift in Treasury
themes.description: The evolving treasury landscape demands a significant shift in skills and mindset. Treasurers need to be not only financially astute but also technically fluent, cross-functionally agile, and effective communicators. The transformation is moving cash flow from a finance-only responsibility to a company-wide mission, requiring greater collaboration across departments and a culture that prioritizes cash visibility and control.
themes.key_stat: 38.5% of respondents cite difficulties in standardising processes as their most significant obstacle to centralisation

themes.name: Risk Management & Compliance
themes.description: Fraud prevention, ESG reporting, and adherence to regulations like ISO 20022 are critical priorities. The increasing risk of fraud, particularly with instant payments, necessitates robust controls, real-time monitoring, and employee education. ESG is becoming embedded in financing strategies and reporting obligations, while ISO 20022 demands structured data for improved compliance screening and end-to-end payment visibility.
themes.key_stat: More than a quarter of treasurers (27.6%) list fraud prevention as a priority.

themes.name: Virtual Accounts & In-House Banking
themes.description: Virtual accounts have become a mainstream treasury tool, offering simplified account structures, faster reconciliation, and sharper liquidity insights. Their adoption is rising as corporates seek to reduce physical accounts and segregate flows by business unit or purpose. In-house banks (IHBs) are also gaining traction as a means to centralize cash, automate intercompany settlements, and reduce reliance on external banking infrastructure.
themes.key_stat: 17% of corporates now use virtual accounts primarily for reconciling incoming payments, up five to six percentage points from two years ago.

key_actions.rationale: The report emphasizes the critical need for real-time visibility and instant payments for effective cash management and working capital optimization. CMIplus must ensure its platform fully supports instant payment processing, real-time reporting via Open APIs, and virtual account capabilities across all channels (EBICS, H2H, SWIFT, Web, Mobile) and network banks in CEE to meet evolving corporate demands and regulatory mandates (e.g., EU Instant Payments Regulation).
key_actions.timeline: Immediate focus on API-based real-time data feeds and virtual account enhancements; continuous development for full instant payment scheme compliance by 2025/26.

key_actions.action: Proactive Support for Verification of Payee (VoP)
key_actions.rationale: VoP is a significant regulatory change (October 2025 deadline) aimed at fraud reduction, but it presents practical challenges for corporates, especially with virtual accounts and COBO structures. CMIplus needs to offer clear guidance, robust validation tools, and flexible solutions that integrate VoP checks seamlessly into payment workflows, minimizing disruption for clients and ensuring compliance across multi-currency payments and CEE markets.
key_actions.timeline: Develop and integrate VoP validation services into CMIplus by early 2025; provide client education and support materials.

key_actions.action: Drive ISO 20022 Adoption and Structured Data Capabilities
key_actions.rationale: ISO 20022 is a strategic upgrade for structured data, improved visibility, and automation, moving beyond mere compliance. CMIplus should actively promote and facilitate clients' transition to ISO 20022 native formats, ensuring the platform can handle richer payment data, support LEIs, and enable straight-through processing. This will future-proof payment flows and reduce exceptions for large international corporates in CEE.
key_actions.timeline: Ongoing support for ISO 20022 migration; actively encourage clients to adopt structured data practices by 2025/26.

key_actions.action: Integrate AI for Enhanced Forecasting and Automation
key_actions.rationale: AI is transitioning from hype to practical application in treasury, particularly for cash flow forecasting, fraud detection, and workflow automation. CMIplus can differentiate by offering AI-powered insights and automation features, helping CEE corporates improve cash flow precision and operational efficiency. This aligns with the report's emphasis on moving treasury to a more strategic role, provided clean data foundations are in place.
key_actions.timeline: Pilot AI-driven forecasting and anomaly detection features in 2025; develop a roadmap for broader AI integration into CMIplus services by 2026-2027.

competitive_implications: The report highlights that banks must adapt to a rapidly evolving payment landscape driven by real-time transactions, new regulations (VoP, Instant Payments), and emerging technologies (AI, APIs, virtual accounts). For CMIplus, this means a critical need to not only meet baseline compliance for these changes but to proactively offer integrated, user-friendly solutions that simplify complexity for large international corporates in CEE. Failure to do so risks losing ground to competitors who provide more advanced tools for real-time liquidity, fraud prevention, and data-driven decision-making, especially given the emphasis on 'symphony of systems' and 'strategic partners'.

case_studies.headline: Dialling Up Cash Flow at Vodafone
case_studies.key_achievement: Transformed cash flow into a company-wide mission, embedding a cash-conscious mindset across all functions and implementing real-time receivables dashboards to improve visibility and decision-making, ultimately reducing unproductive, bound capital.
case_studies.lesson: Successful cash flow transformation requires strong top-down support, cross-functional alignment, cultural change, and clear data visibility. It's a company-wide mission, not just a treasury task, and demands dedicated resources beyond the treasury team.

case_studies.headline: From Complexity to Clarity: DEME's Evolving Treasury Journey
case_studies.key_achievement: Centralized treasury operations from decentralized roots, significantly reducing bank accounts, implementing a central payment factory, and embedding sanctions screening earlier in the transaction lifecycle. Also transformed long-term loans into sustainability-linked structures.
case_studies.lesson: Centralization requires strict procedures to maintain consistency as the business grows. Proactive risk management (e.g., early sanctions screening) is more effective than gatekeeping. ESG integration is becoming a core element of financing strategy, positioning treasury as a strategic partner.

case_studies.headline: Treasury Automation in Action at Evonik
case_studies.key_achievement: Embedded automation at the core of its operations, achieving near-total payment straight-through processing (99% automated) and developing an in-house real-time treasury cockpit for consolidated financial insights. Successfully streamlined FX exposure management.
case_studies.lesson: Technology should be a strategic partner, not just a tool for efficiency. A fully integrated platform provides a single source of truth, enabling faster decision-making and freeing up time for strategic tasks. Strong governance and data standardization are essential, and treasurers must own the transformation from the start.

case_studies.headline: Banking on Change: Inside Comcast's Treasury Transformation
case_studies.key_achievement: Overhauled a fragmented 'Frankenstein' banking landscape into a unified global liquidity framework, closing over 2,000 bank accounts, consolidating with strategic partners, and making over 80% of on-hand cash accessible. This significantly reduced commercial paper borrowings.
case_studies.lesson: Large-scale treasury transformation requires persistence, a clear vision (e.g., optimizing global liquidity), strong executive sponsorship, and a nuanced region-by-region approach to navigate regulatory and cultural hurdles. It also serves as a proving ground for talent development, fostering critical thinking and problem-solving.

case_studies.headline: Racing the Clock and Winning! How Accell Group Built an In-House Bank in Just Three Months
case_studies.key_achievement: Rapidly designed and implemented a semi-automated in-house bank (IHB) in just three months, replacing a strained notional cash pool. The IHB manages POBO, intercompany non-cash settlements, automated sweeps, and ERP-integrated reporting, restoring liquidity control under pressure.
case_studies.lesson: Crisis can drive rapid transformation. A lean, focused team, strong external partnerships, and a pragmatic approach (preserving existing interfaces where possible) are crucial for fast-paced, successful project delivery. Automation of sweeps and intercompany settlements improves cash efficiency and visibility.

case_studies.headline: Rewiring Treasury at Zoetis
case_studies.key_achievement: Built a lean, centralized, digitally enabled treasury function since its spin-off, achieving global cash visibility, automating processes (reconciliation, reporting, forecasting), and adopting end-to-end payment tracking via Swift GPI. Utilizes AI for payment screening and exception reporting.
case_studies.lesson: Lasting treasury transformation begins with a clear purpose rooted in real pain points, not just technology. Starting small, staying flexible, and involving the team throughout the journey is key. Efficiency gains free up time for strategic analysis and allow treasury to communicate its value more clearly to the wider business.
